diagnosis.summary: Your onions are likely rotting either in the shamba or during storage, which produces a foul odor.
likely_causes: Bacterial soft rot caused by too much water in the soil or poor drainage.
Neck rot disease which occurs when onions are harvested in wet weather and not dried properly.
Pest damage from soil insects that cuts the bulbs and allows rot to enter.
diagnosis.recommended_approach: Immediately sort through your onions to remove and bury all rotting ones, then dry the healthy ones in a well-ventilated, shaded place.

this_week_actions: Dig up all smelling onions and separate them from the healthy ones immediately.
Bury the rotten onions in a deep pit far away from your farming field.
Spread the healthy onions on a dry, shaded, and well-ventilated surface to cure.
Stop watering the remaining onion beds immediately to let the soil dry out.
materials_needed: A spade or jembe to dig a disposal pit.
Dry cardboard sheets or clean sacks to spread out the drying onions.
A hand hoe to dig drainage channels in wet onion beds.
warning_signs: More than half of the remaining onions turn soft and mushy within three days.
You find white maggots actively feeding inside the necks of healthy-looking onions.
action_plan.expected_outcome: The rot will stop spreading, and the remaining healthy onions will dry out completely within two weeks.
